config.serverPath.description: Path to the poly binary. Relative paths resolve against the first workspace folder; empty uses the bundled binary, then `poly` from PATH.
config.tools.description: Where poly gets each external tool, by tool name: the `[tools]` table of poly.toml, for the editor. Without an entry poly uses the tool on PATH when its major version matches poly's pin, and downloads its own otherwise. A value is `"off"`, `"on"`, a version to download instead (PATH is then skipped), or the absolute path of a binary, for example `{ "shellcheck": "off", "tflint": "0.53.0" }`. Applies to poly's language server, the PlantUML jar, and `poly check` and dead-code analysis in the terminal. A tool named here overrides the same tool in poly.toml, which still applies to every other tool and is all the command line reads. Changing this restarts the language server.
config.lintOnSave.description: Publish lint diagnostics when a supported file is opened or saved. Takes effect immediately. The Lint switch in the status bar (`Poly: Toggle Linting`) turns this off together with the linters of other installed extensions -- ruff, Go's lint and vet on save, rust-analyzer's check on save, Code Spell Checker, autocorrect, ESLint, ShellCheck, Stylelint, Pylint, Flake8 -- and puts every one of them back as it was when switched on again. Compile and type errors are not lint and stay. Editing this setting directly affects poly alone.
config.format.enabled.description: Let poly rewrite files: Format Document, format-on-save, Format Selection, and the trailing-whitespace and final-newline fixes .editorconfig asks for on save. The Format switch in the status bar (`Poly: Toggle Formatting`) turns this off together with every automatic rewrite in the editor: format on save, type and paste, code actions on save, trailing whitespace and final newline, including the per-language defaults other extensions ship (golang.go's `[go]` format-on-save, Pylance's `[python]` format-on-type), and puts every one of them back as it was when switched on again. It writes your user settings only; a workspace's own settings that turn formatting on are named in the switch's tooltip rather than changed. Format Document run by hand with another extension's formatter still works. Linting is unaffected. Editing this setting directly affects poly alone. The format shortcut (`Poly: Format Document`, shift+alt+f) formats regardless of this setting and of the switch.
config.deadCodeCodeLens.enabled.descript: Show an `analyze dead code` link on the first line of code in every file poly can answer about: Go (golang.org/x/tools/cmd/deadcode), TypeScript and JavaScript (knip), Python (vulture). Clicking it runs `poly deadcode` in a terminal over that file's whole project — the go.work build list, the npm project, the Python project. Nothing runs until it is clicked: whole-program reachability costs a build, so it is asked rather than watched.
config.memoryLog.description: Write a line to the Poly output channel every time a file is opened or closed, saying what the daemon is holding: resident memory, how many documents and how many bytes of text, the lint and package caches, the findings each source is keeping, and which language servers are running. Off by default — it is a line per file in a log you also read to find out why a lint did not run. Turn it on when poly's memory looks wrong: the point of the line is that a rising number can be blamed on one of the caches rather than left as "the daemon got bigger". Read once at startup, so it takes a window reload.
config.updateCheck.enabled.description: Periodically check GitHub Releases for new Poly versions, and install a new one without asking; only the window reload is left to you. An update installs poly-syntax-highlight too when it is installed, and that extension also checks on its own schedule (poly.syntax.updateCheck.*); a release one of the two already installed in this window is not installed again.
config.updateCheck.intervalDays.descript: Days between automatic update checks; 0 checks on every startup.

config.indentTint.enabled.description: Tint each level of leading whitespace, and mark whitespace that does not fill a level -- a mixed tab/space line shows up as a partial band rather than as nothing. Costs one set of decorations per visible line; nothing is scanned outside the viewport. Colours are the poly.indentLevel1-4 and poly.indentPartial theme colours, each overridable in workbench.colorCustomizations.
config.imagePreview.enabled.description: Show a thumbnail in the gutter for lines that name an image file which exists. Only lines on screen are resolved, and only paths that resolve to a real file in the workspace; a URL or a missing file draws nothing. Costs one file read per distinct image.
config.unicodeHighlight.enabled.descript: Mark characters that are not what they look like -- invisible and bidirectional controls, spaces that are not U+0020, and lookalikes such as an en dash or a curly quote -- in every file and as you type, the way the gremlins extension does: a mark in the gutter, a tick in the scrollbar, the character's name at the end of its line, and a hover saying why it is marked. Levels follow gremlins, and the colours are the poly.unicodeError, poly.unicodeWarning and poly.unicodeInfo theme colours, each overridable in workbench.colorCustomizations. The Problems entries for the same characters come from the poly/unicode-* rules, which run on save and are what `poly: ignore` and poly.toml silence; this highlight only shows, and neither of them turns it off.
config.referencesCodeLens.enabled.descri: Show a reference count above each declaration, an implementation count above each type and method -- `N impls` over an interface (who satisfies it) and `N interfaces` over a concrete type (what it satisfies, left out when that is nothing) -- and `N methods` over a type whose methods are declared outside it, as Go's are. Every count comes from whatever reference provider the language already has; poly analyses nothing, so a language with no provider gets no lens. Costs one reference query per declaration scrolled into view, and the answer is reused for ten seconds so that typing does not ask again. Clicking any of these lenses goes straight there when there is one place to go, and opens the references list when there are several.
config.protobufCodeLens.enabled.descript: Link a .proto declaration to the Go protoc generated for it: `go type` over a message or enum, `go server` and `go client` over a service, and an implementation count over each rpc. A click goes straight there when there is one place to go and opens the references list when there are several, without leaving the .proto. The lens is drawn only when the generated file is already in the workspace and holds the declaration, so nothing points at a file that has not been generated yet. Needs another extension to provide the .proto outline, such as Buf (`bufbuild.vscode-buf`), which runs `buf lsp serve`. Covers protoc-gen-go and protoc-gen-go-grpc; connect-go and other generators name their output in ways the proto does not predict and are left alone.
config.runCodeLens.enabled.description: Show `run | debug` above a program's entry point -- `main` in Go, Rust, C, C++ and Java, `Main` in C#, `if __name__ == "__main__"` in Python, and the shebang of a shell script. `run` saves the file and runs it the way Code Runner's Run Code does, with its settings (poly.codeRunner.*): in the Output panel, or in a terminal with poly.codeRunner.runInTerminal. It appears wherever those settings have a command for the file, whether or not poly.codeRunner.enabled is on. `debug` hands over to whichever debug extension is installed for the language, exactly as F5 would. poly ships no debugger.
config.codeRunner.enabled.description: Do what Code Runner (formulahendry.code-runner) does: **Run Code** (`ctrl+alt+n`) runs the file, or the selected code, with the command the settings below give its language; **Run Custom Command** (`ctrl+alt+k`), **Run By Language** (`ctrl+alt+j`) and **Stop Code Run** (`ctrl+alt+m`) are there too, with the ▶ in the editor title and the editor's and the Explorer's context menus. Off, none of them shows. The `run` lens (`#poly.runCodeLens.enabled#`) runs with these settings either way. While formulahendry.code-runner is installed, poly stands aside.
config.codeRunner.executorMapByGlob.desc: The command for files whose name matches a glob, checked before the language's. The placeholders of `#poly.codeRunner.executorMap#` work here too.
config.codeRunner.executorMap.descriptio: The command each language is run with, by language id. The file's quoted path goes on the end unless the command places it with a placeholder: `$fullFileName` (the quoted path), `$fileName`, `$fileNameWithoutExt`, `$dir` (the quoted folder, ending in a separator), `$dirWithoutTrailingSlash`, `$workspaceRoot`, `$driveLetter` (Windows) and `$pythonPath` (the interpreter the Python extension has selected; without it `python3`, and `python` on Windows). Go and Rust run their package, `go run .` and `cargo run` in the file's folder, and Python runs through `$pythonPath`; every other default is Code Runner's.
config.codeRunner.executorMapByFileExten: The command by file extension, dot included (`.vbs`), for a file whose language has none in `#poly.codeRunner.executorMap#`.
config.codeRunner.customCommand.descript: What **Run Custom Command** runs. The placeholders of `#poly.codeRunner.executorMap#` refer to the file in the editor, and nothing is put on the end.
config.codeRunner.languageIdToFileExtens: The extension of the temporary file a selection or an unsaved file is run from, by language id. Without an entry it is the file's own.
config.codeRunner.defaultLanguage.descri: The language id whose command runs a file no setting has a command for, such as `javascript`. Empty runs nothing.
config.codeRunner.cwd.description: The working directory of a run in the Output panel. Empty is the file's workspace folder -- the file's own folder with `#poly.codeRunner.fileDirectoryAsCwd#` or outside a workspace -- and the system's temporary folder when there is neither.
config.codeRunner.fileDirectoryAsCwd.des: Run in the file's own folder rather than its workspace folder. In a terminal, `cd` there first.
config.codeRunner.clearPreviousOutput.de: Clear the Output panel, or the terminal, before each run.
Save every file before a run.
config.codeRunner.saveFileBeforeRun.desc: Save the file before running it. Off, a run is of the file as last saved. The `run` lens always saves first.
config.codeRunner.showExecutionMessage.d: Write `[Running]` and the command before a run's output, and `[Done]` with its exit code and time after it.
config.codeRunner.runInTerminal.descript: Run in a terminal named Code Runner instead of the Output panel. A program that reads input needs this, since the Output panel has no stdin. **Stop Code Run** does not reach a terminal; `ctrl+c` does.
config.codeRunner.terminalRoot.descripti: Windows only: with a Unix shell such as Bash or Cygwin as the terminal, the root that replaces a drive letter in the command -- `/mnt/` turns `C:\path` into `/mnt/c/path`.
config.codeRunner.preserveFocus.descript: Keep the focus in the editor when a run starts. Off, the Output panel or the terminal takes it.
config.codeRunner.ignoreSelection.descri: Always run the whole file, even with code selected.
config.codeRunner.showRunIconInEditorTit: Show **Run Code** in the editor title's ▶ menu.
config.codeRunner.showStopIconInEditorTi: Show **Stop Code Run** in the editor title while a run is going.
config.codeRunner.showRunCommandInEditor: Show **Run Code** in the editor's context menu.
config.codeRunner.showRunCommandInExplor: Show **Run Code** in the Explorer's context menu.
config.codeRunner.temporaryFileName.desc: The name, without its extension, of the temporary file selected code is run from. It is written beside the file and deleted after a run in the Output panel. Empty picks a random name.
config.codeRunner.respectShebang.descrip: Run a file whose first line is a shebang (`#!/usr/bin/env python3`) with the command it names, before any other setting is asked. `#![` is Rust's, not a shebang.
config.markdownMermaid.enabled.descripti: Render ```mermaid fences as diagrams in the markdown preview. Ignored on VSCode 1.135 and later, which ships the same renderer as a built-in (mermaid-markdown-features): poly stands down rather than draw a second diagram over the first.
config.postfixCompletion.enabled.descrip: Offer postfix templates after a dot: `err.if` expands to `if err != nil { }` in Go, `if (err) { }` in TypeScript, `if err:` in Python. Covers go, rust, swift, typescript, javascript (and their react variants), python, lua, c and cpp. These are text templates, not analysis -- poly reads the characters left of the dot and rearranges them -- and they sort after whatever the language server offered, so they never displace a real completion.
config.todo.enabled.description: Show the TODOs view in the Explorer. The view scans the workspace for the markers in poly.todo.tags, and only while it is on screen -- a closed view costs nothing. Capped at 4000 files and 512KB per file, and it says so when it stops early.
config.todo.tags.description: Markers the TODOs view lists. Matched as whole words, case-sensitively; entries that are not plain words are ignored.
config.syntaxColors.description: Syntax colours of your own, over the theme's. Item is a TextMate scope (`comment`, `keyword.control.rust`), value is a colour with optional styles (`#C586C0`, `#6A9955 italic`, `bold`). A scope also colours the longer scopes under it, so `comment` covers every kind of comment. To find a scope's name, run **Poly: Set Syntax Color** in a file (it lists every scope that file's grammar has and writes the entry here), **Poly: Syntax Colors for This Language** for the whole list, or **Developer: Inspect Editor Tokens and Scopes** for the one under the cursor. poly copies these into `editor.tokenColorCustomizations` as rules named `poly.syntaxColors` -- that is the only thing a theme reads -- and leaves rules you wrote there yourself alone.
config.syntaxColors.pattern: A colour like #C586C0, optionally followed by bold, italic, underline or strikethrough
config.autocorrect.enabled.description: Do what the AutoCorrect extension (huacnlee.autocorrect) does, with its own engine: spaces between CJK and Latin text, full- and half-width punctuation, and spelling of the words in `.autocorrectrc`. Findings appear as you open and type, each with a quick fix; a manual save corrects the whole file; **Poly: AutoCorrect: Format Document** does it by hand. `.autocorrectrc` and `.autocorrectignore` (plus `.gitignore`) are read from the workspace folder. While huacnlee.autocorrect is installed, poly stands aside. The Lint and Format switches in the status bar turn these off with everything else.
config.autocorrect.enableLint.descriptio: Report AutoCorrect findings in the Problems panel, as you open and type.
config.autocorrect.formatOnSave.descript: Correct the whole file on a manual save. Auto-save does not trigger it, and Save without Formatting skips it.
color.indentLevel1.description: Background of the first indent level.
color.indentLevel2.description: Background of the second indent level.
color.indentLevel3.description: Background of the third indent level.
color.indentLevel4.description: Background of the fourth indent level; levels beyond it cycle.
color.indentPartial.description: Background of leading whitespace that does not fill an indent level.
color.unicodeError.description: Unicode highlight: bidirectional controls and invisible characters, which can change what code means without showing it.
color.unicodeWarning.description: Unicode highlight: lookalikes such as an en dash or a curly quote, and the few control characters gremlins ranks as warnings.
color.unicodeInfo.description: Unicode highlight: spaces that are not U+0020, and the soft hyphen.

config.markdownDiagrams.enabled.descript: Draw ```nomnoml, ```flowchart (or ```flow), ```sequence, ```vega, ```vega-lite, ```markmap and ```excalidraw (a scene's JSON) fences as diagrams in the markdown preview. Each library is loaded the first time a document uses it. ```plantuml (or ```puml, ```uml) fences are drawn with the settings under poly.plantuml: by poly.plantuml.server when one is set, otherwise with Java on this machine.
config.markdownGithubStyle.enabled.descr: Style the markdown preview like GitHub, as the Markdown Preview Github Styling extension (bierner.markdown-preview-github-styles) does. Ignored while that extension is installed, since it already does this.
config.markdownGithubStyle.colorTheme.de: Which of the two GitHub themes below the preview uses.
config.markdownGithubStyle.colorTheme.sy: Follow the operating system's light or dark setting.
config.markdownGithubStyle.colorTheme.li: Always use the light theme below.
config.markdownGithubStyle.colorTheme.da: Always use the dark theme below.
config.markdownGithubStyle.lightTheme.de: GitHub theme for light mode. Unused when `#poly.markdownGithubStyle.colorTheme#` is `dark`.
config.markdownGithubStyle.darkTheme.des: GitHub theme for dark mode. Unused when `#poly.markdownGithubStyle.colorTheme#` is `light`.

config.plantuml.enabled.description: Do what jebbs.plantuml does: the preview, export and server-URL commands, extracting the source from an exported PNG, and completion, signature help, the outline and the checks in PlantUML files. ```plantuml fences in the markdown preview are drawn only while this is on as well. Off hides the commands and stops the language features. jebbs.plantuml, while installed, does all of this itself.
config.plantuml.java.description: The Java that runs PlantUML. poly downloads the jar (or runs the one `plantuml` in `poly.tools`, or `[tools]` in poly.toml, points at) but not Java: where `java` is not on PATH, point this at one.
config.plantuml.commandArgs.description: Arguments for the `java` command, before `-jar`, such as `-DPLANTUML_LIMIT_SIZE=8192`.
config.plantuml.jarArgs.description: Arguments for PlantUML itself, after the jar, such as `-config plantuml.config`.
config.plantuml.includepaths.description: Folders `!include` searches besides the diagram's own folder and `#poly.plantuml.diagramsRoot#`. Relative ones are relative to the workspace folder.
config.plantuml.diagramsRoot.description: Where the workspace's diagrams live, relative to the workspace folder. Export Workspace PlantUML Diagrams starts here, `!include` searches here, and exports keep the folders below it.
config.plantuml.fileExtensions.descripti: The files Export Workspace PlantUML Diagrams looks in, comma-separated. Add `.java` or `.md` to export diagrams written in comments or documents.
config.plantuml.exportFormat.description: Export format. Empty asks every time.
config.plantuml.exportOutDir.description: Where exports go, relative to the workspace folder.
config.plantuml.exportSubFolder.descript: Export each file's diagrams into a folder named after the file.
config.plantuml.exportIncludeFolderHiera: Keep the folders between `#poly.plantuml.diagramsRoot#` and the file in the export path.
config.plantuml.exportConcurrency.descri: How many diagrams render at once on this machine. Each is a Java process; the markdown preview keeps to the same limit.
config.plantuml.exportMapFile.descriptio: Export each diagram's image map (`.cmapx`) beside it.
config.plantuml.previewAutoUpdate.descri: Redraw the preview as the diagram is edited, and when the cursor moves into another diagram.
config.plantuml.previewSnapIndicators.de: Show the snap indicators in the preview.
Swap the mouse buttons for zooming and panning in the preview.
config.plantuml.server.description: A PlantUML server, for the URL commands, for `#poly.plantuml.render#` set to `PlantUMLServer`, and, when set, for the markdown preview's fences. The public one is `https://www.plantuml.com/plantuml`; what is sent there leaves this machine.
config.plantuml.urlFormat.description: Format of generated URLs. Empty asks every time.
config.plantuml.urlResult.description: Generated URLs as markdown images, or as bare URLs.
config.plantuml.render.description: Who draws previews and exports: `Local` runs the jar with Java on this machine; `PlantUMLServer` sends the diagram to `#poly.plantuml.server#`, which is faster and needs no Java.
config.plantuml.lintDiagramNoName.descri: Warn about a diagram with no name after `@startuml`. Its exports are named after the file and its position in it, which changes when diagrams are added above it.

config.markdownPdf.enabled.description: Do what yzane.markdown-pdf does: the **Export Markdown** commands (PDF, HTML, PNG, JPEG) and `poly.markdownPdf.convertOnSave`. Off hides the commands and stops converting on save. yzane.markdown-pdf, while installed, takes over.
config.markdownPdf.type.description: The formats that **Export Markdown (settings.json)** and convert-on-save write: any of `pdf`, `html`, `png` and `jpeg`.
config.markdownPdf.convertOnSave.descrip: Export a markdown file each time it is saved, to the formats in `#poly.markdownPdf.type#`.
Regular expressions for file names that `#poly.markdownPdf.convertOnSave#` skips.
config.markdownPdf.outputDirectory.descr: The folder exports are written to. Empty writes them next to the markdown file. `~` is the home folder, and an absolute folder must already exist. A relative path is from the workspace folder, or from the file's folder with `#poly.markdownPdf.outputDirectoryRelativePathFile#`.
config.markdownPdf.outputDirectoryRelati: Resolve a relative `#poly.markdownPdf.outputDirectory#` from the markdown file's folder instead of the workspace folder.
config.markdownPdf.sanitize.description: Which raw HTML in the markdown is removed before rendering. `gfm` removes the tags GitHub removes, such as `script`, `iframe` and `style`. `gfm-allow-style` keeps `<style>` for page layout, but CSS can still send data out through `url()` and `@import`, so use it only with content you trust. `none` removes nothing and is not recommended.
config.markdownPdf.styles.description: Stylesheets added after the default ones: local paths or `http`, `https` and `data` URLs. A relative path is from the workspace folder, or from the file's folder with `#poly.markdownPdf.stylesRelativePathFile#`.
config.markdownPdf.stylesRelativePathFil: Resolve relative paths in `#poly.markdownPdf.styles#` from the markdown file's folder instead of the workspace folder.
Include the default styles: VSCode's markdown preview stylesheet, markdown-pdf's own, and the stylesheets in `#markdown.styles#`.
config.markdownPdf.highlight.description: Highlight the syntax in code blocks.
config.markdownPdf.highlightStyle.descri: The [highlight.js theme](https://highlightjs.org/demo) for code blocks, by file name. Empty uses Tomorrow.
config.markdownPdf.breaks.description:
Turn each line break inside a paragraph into `
`.
config.markdownPdf.emoji.description: Turn `:name:` into its emoji, drawn as the character in the system's emoji font. A name that has no character, such as `:octocat:`, stays as written.
config.markdownPdf.executablePath.descri: The Chrome, Chromium or Edge that PDF, PNG and JPEG export runs. Empty uses an installed Chrome or Edge, or else the Chrome for Testing that Poly downloads.
config.markdownPdf.chromium.autoDownload: When no browser is set or installed, download the Chrome for Testing build that Poly pins the first time an export needs it, and check its digest. Off, nothing is downloaded, and PDF, PNG and JPEG export need `#poly.markdownPdf.executablePath#` or an installed browser.
config.markdownPdf.scale.description: Scale of the page rendering, from 0.1 to 2.
config.markdownPdf.displayHeaderFooter.d: PDF only. Print the header and the footer.
config.markdownPdf.headerTemplate.descri: PDF only. The header's HTML. Elements with the class `date`, `title`, `url`, `pageNumber` or `totalPages` get that value.
config.markdownPdf.footerTemplate.descri: PDF only. The footer's HTML. Elements with the class `date`, `title`, `url`, `pageNumber` or `totalPages` get that value.
config.markdownPdf.printBackground.descr: PDF only. Print background colors and images.
config.markdownPdf.pageRanges.descriptio: PDF only. The pages to print, such as `1-5, 8, 11-13`. Empty prints them all.
config.markdownPdf.format.description: PDF only. Paper size. `#poly.markdownPdf.width#` or `#poly.markdownPdf.height#` overrides it.
config.markdownPdf.width.description: PDF only. Paper width, with a unit: `mm`, `cm`, `in` or `px`. Overrides `#poly.markdownPdf.format#`.
config.markdownPdf.height.description: PDF only. Paper height, with a unit: `mm`, `cm`, `in` or `px`. Overrides `#poly.markdownPdf.format#`.
config.markdownPdf.margin.top.descriptio: PDF only. The top margin, with a unit: `mm`, `cm`, `in` or `px`.
config.markdownPdf.margin.bottom.descrip: PDF only. The bottom margin, with a unit: `mm`, `cm`, `in` or `px`.
config.markdownPdf.margin.right.descript: PDF only. The right margin, with a unit: `mm`, `cm`, `in` or `px`.
config.markdownPdf.margin.left.descripti: PDF only. The left margin, with a unit: `mm`, `cm`, `in` or `px`.
config.markdownPdf.quality.description: JPEG only. Image quality, from 0 to 100.
config.markdownPdf.clip.x.description: PNG and JPEG only. Left edge of the area to capture, in pixels. Unless all four clip settings are set, the whole page is captured.
config.markdownPdf.clip.y.description: PNG and JPEG only. Top edge of the area to capture, in pixels. Unless all four clip settings are set, the whole page is captured.
config.markdownPdf.clip.width.descriptio: PNG and JPEG only. Width of the area to capture, in pixels. Unless all four clip settings are set, the whole page is captured.
config.markdownPdf.clip.height.descripti: PNG and JPEG only. Height of the area to capture, in pixels. Unless all four clip settings are set, the whole page is captured.
config.markdownPdf.omitBackground.descri: PNG and JPEG only. Leave out the default white background, so that the image can be transparent.
config.markdownPdf.plantumlOpenMarker.de: The line that opens a PlantUML diagram.
config.markdownPdf.plantumlCloseMarker.d: The line that closes a PlantUML diagram.
config.markdownPdf.plantumlServer.descri: The PlantUML server that draws the diagrams. Each diagram's source is sent to it.
config.markdownPdf.StatusbarMessageTimeo: How long the status bar shows the exported file, in milliseconds.
config.markdownPdf.markdown-it-include.e: Replace `:[alt](file.md)` with the contents of that file.
config.markdownPdf.mermaidServer.descrip: Where the exported page loads mermaid from, to draw `mermaid` blocks.
config.markdownPdf.math.enabled.descript: Render math with KaTeX, as VSCode's preview does: `$…$`, `$$…$$`, `\(…\)`, `\[…\]` and `math` blocks. Off leaves them as written.

command.codeSnap.title: CodeSnap 📸
config.codeSnap.enabled.description: Do what adpyke.codesnap does: **CodeSnap** turns the selected code into an image. Off hides the command. adpyke.codesnap, while installed, takes over.
config.codeSnap.backgroundColor.descript: The color around the window in the picture, as CSS.
config.codeSnap.boxShadow.description: The window's shadow, as a CSS `box-shadow`.
config.codeSnap.containerPadding.descrip: The space between the window and the picture's edge, as a CSS `padding`.
config.codeSnap.showWindowTitle.descript: Title the window with the workspace's name and the file's.
config.codeSnap.realLineNumbers.descript: Number the lines as the file does, rather than from 1.
config.codeSnap.transparentBackground.de: Leave the area around the window transparent in the picture.
config.codeSnap.target.description: What the picture shows: `container`, the window and the area around it, or `window`, the window alone on a transparent background.
config.codeSnap.shutterAction.descriptio: What the shutter button does: `save` asks where to save the PNG, `copy` puts it on the clipboard. Copying in the page (Cmd+C or Ctrl+C) always copies it.
command.pasteImage.title: Paste Image
config.pasteImage.enabled.description: Do what mushan.vscode-paste-image does: **Paste Image** saves the image on the clipboard to a file and inserts a link to it. Off hides the command and frees its key. vscode-paste-image, while installed, takes over.
config.pasteImage.path.description: The folder the pasted image is saved in: absolute, or from the folder of the file being pasted into. `${currentFileDir}` is that folder, `${projectRoot}` the workspace folder it is in, `${currentFileName}` and `${currentFileNameWithoutExt}` its name.
config.pasteImage.basePath.description: The folder the inserted path is relative to, with the same variables as `#poly.pasteImage.path#`. Empty inserts the absolute path.
config.pasteImage.forceUnixStyleSeparato: Separate the inserted path with `/` on Windows too.
config.pasteImage.prefix.description: Text put before the inserted path.
config.pasteImage.suffix.description: Text put after the inserted path.
config.pasteImage.defaultName.descriptio: The image's name when no text is selected (selected text is the name otherwise): the time it was pasted, in a [moment.js format](https://momentjs.com/docs/#/displaying/format/). The variables of `#poly.pasteImage.path#` work here too.
config.pasteImage.namePrefix.description: Text put before the image's file name.
config.pasteImage.nameSuffix.description: Text put after the image's file name, before `.png`.
config.pasteImage.encodePath.description: How the inserted path is encoded: `none`, `urlEncode` as a URL, or `urlEncodeSpace` with only spaces as `%20`.
config.pasteImage.insertPattern.descript: What is inserted. `${imageFilePath}` is the path after prefix, suffix and encoding, `${imageOriginalFilePath}` the path without them, `${imageFileName}` and `${imageFileNameWithoutExt}` the name, and `${imageSyntaxPrefix}`/`${imageSyntaxSuffix}` markdown's `![](`/`)` or AsciiDoc's `image::`/`[]` in those files and nothing elsewhere. The variables of `#poly.pasteImage.path#` work here too.
config.pasteImage.showFilePathConfirmInp: Ask for the image's path before saving it.
config.pasteImage.filePathConfirmInputBo: What `#poly.pasteImage.showFilePathConfirmInputBox#` asks for: `fullPath`, the whole path, or `onlyName`, the file name alone.

config.dataPreview.theme.description: Data Preview's look: `light`, `dark`, their compact `dense.light` and `dense.dark`, or `vaporwave`, a high-contrast blue.
config.dataPreview.create.json.files.des: Write the rows of an Arrow, Avro, Parquet or Excel file to a `.json` beside it when it is previewed. A file already there is left alone.
config.dataPreview.create.json.schema.de: Write the columns of an Arrow or Avro file to a `.schema.json` beside it when it is previewed. A file already there is left alone.
config.dataPreview.openSavedFileEditor.d: Open the file Data Preview saves in an editor.

config.swaggerViewer.defaultHost.descrip: The host the preview is served on.
config.swaggerViewer.defaultPort.descrip: The port the preview is served on, or the next free one after it. Read when the preview server starts.
config.swaggerViewer.previewInBrowser.de: Open the preview in the browser rather than in the editor.
config.swaggerViewer.showOnlyFileName.de: Title the preview with the file's name alone, rather than its whole path.
config.swaggerViewer.zoomLevel.descripti: The preview's zoom, in percent (50 to 200).
config.marp.breaks.off: Join the lines, as Markdown does.
config.marp.breaks.on: Break the line. Marp's own default.
config.marp.enabled.description: Do what marp-team.marp-vscode does: Markdown with `marp: true` in its front matter becomes slides in the preview, with Marp's diagnostics, completion and export. Off shows those documents as ordinary Markdown and hides the Marp commands. marp-vscode, while installed, takes over.
config.marp.breaks.description: How a line break inside a paragraph renders in a Marp slide. Marp's default differs from VSCode's preview, so it is set apart from it.
config.marp.browser.auto: Whichever of Chrome, Chromium, Edge or Firefox is found.
config.marp.browser.description: The installed browser that exports PDF, PPTX and images.
config.marp.browserPath.description: The browser that exports PDF, PPTX and images. `#poly.marp.browser#` says which kind it is. Empty, an installed one is found.
config.marp.diagnostics.slideContentOver: Warn when a slide's content overflows the area inside its padding. Only while the Markdown preview is open, since the preview is what measures it.
config.marp.exportType.description: The export dialog's default file type.
config.marp.exportAutoOpen.description: Open the exported file in the application the operating system assigns to it.
config.marp.html.off: None, not even the ones Marp allows.
config.marp.html.all: All of them, which makes rendering a deck you did not write unsafe.
config.marp.html.description: Which HTML elements in Marp Markdown render in the slides.
config.marp.mathTypesetting.off: No math syntax, and no `math` directive.
config.marp.mathTypesetting.description: Math syntax, and the library that renders it in [Marp Core](https://github.com/marp-team/marp-core). A deck can pick the other one with the `math` global directive. `#markdown.math.enabled#` does not apply to Marp Markdown.
config.marp.openExportedHtmlInIntegrated: A new tab of the integrated browser.
A new window of the integrated browser.
Open an exported HTML file in [VSCode's integrated browser](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/debugtest/integrated-browser) when `#poly.marp.exportAutoOpen#` is on. Needs VSCode 1.109 or later.
config.marp.outlineExtension.description: List the slides in the Outline view, and let the editor fold each slide's content.
config.marp.pdf.noteAnnotations.descript: Add each slide's [presenter notes](https://marpit.marp.app/usage?id=presenter-notes) to an exported PDF as note annotations.
config.marp.pdf.outlines.both: One per slide, and one per heading.
config.marp.pdf.outlines.description: Add outlines (bookmarks) to an exported PDF, for moving around in a PDF viewer.
config.marp.pptx.editable.off: Never. Each slide is a picture: exact, and with its presenter notes.
config.marp.pptx.editable.on: Always, even though the conversion can fail or lose layout.
config.marp.pptx.editable.smart: Editable first, and pictures if that fails.
config.marp.pptx.editable.description: Export PowerPoint with editable text and shapes. It needs [LibreOffice Impress](https://libreoffice.org/) as well as the browser, and depending on the slides the conversion can fail or lose layout.
config.marp.strictPathResolutionDuringEx: Resolve the relative paths in a deck through the VSCode workspace the file belongs to when exporting. Off, or for a file in no workspace, they resolve on the local file system.
config.marp.themes.description: URLs or paths of extra [theme CSS](https://marpit.marp.app/theme-css) for Marp. Paths follow the rules of `#markdown.styles#`.

config.errorLens.enabled.description: Write each problem's message at the end of its line and tint the line by its severity, with gutter icons, status bar items and code lenses on request: what the Error Lens extension (usernamehw.errorlens) does. The **Poly: Error Lens** commands work while this is off. While usernamehw.errorlens itself is installed and enabled, poly stands aside.
Follow VSCode's `#problems.visibility#`: when it hides problems in the editor, Error Lens hides them too ([VSCode 1.85](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_85#_hide-problem-decorations)). The other keys say which parts follow it.
Show decorations in an editor that has git merge conflict markers (`<<<<<<<`, `=======` or `>>>>>>>`).
config.errorLens.fontFamily.description: Font family of the inline message. Can break `#poly.errorLens.alignMessage#`. [Demo](https://github.com/usernamehw/vscode-error-lens/blob/v3.29.0/docs/docs.md#errorlensfontfamily)
config.errorLens.fontWeight.description: Font weight of the inline message. `normal` is 400 and `bold` is 700. [Demo](https://github.com/usernamehw/vscode-error-lens/blob/v3.29.0/docs/docs.md#errorlensfontweight)
config.errorLens.fontStyleItalic.descrip: Show the inline message in italics. [Demo](https://github.com/usernamehw/vscode-error-lens/blob/v3.29.0/docs/docs.md#errorlensfontstyleitalic)
config.errorLens.fontSize.description: Font size of the inline message, in [CSS units](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/length). A negative value is relative to the editor's font size (`-3px`); empty is the editor's. Can break `#poly.errorLens.alignMessage#`. [Demo](https://github.com/usernamehw/vscode-error-lens/blob/v3.29.0/docs/docs.md#errorlensfontsize)
config.errorLens.margin.description: Space between the end of the line and the inline message, in [CSS units](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/length). [Demo](https://github.com/usernamehw/vscode-error-lens/blob/v3.29.0/docs/docs.md#errorlensmargin)
config.errorLens.alignMessage.minimumMar: Least space, in characters, between the end of the line and an aligned message: what `poly.errorLens.margin` is to messages that are not aligned.
config.errorLens.alignMessage.padding.de: Padding of an aligned message, in characters: top and bottom, then left and right. What `poly.errorLens.padding` is to messages that are not aligned.
config.errorLens.alignMessage.useFixedPo: Pin the message in place, so it does not twitch on the line being typed on. A pinned message cannot be hovered.
config.errorLens.alignMessage.descriptio: Align inline messages to a column: `start` puts each message's start there, `end` its end. Monospace fonts only; both `0` turns it off. Conflicts with other extensions' end-of-line decorations. [Demo](https://github.com/usernamehw/vscode-error-lens/blob/v3.29.0/docs/docs.md#errorlensalignmessage)
config.errorLens.border.description: Border of the inline message, one per severity (error, warning, info, hint): `1px solid`, `1px dashed`, `2px dotted`, `1px solid #00000050`… Empty is none. [Demo](https://github.com/usernamehw/vscode-error-lens/blob/v3.29.0/docs/docs.md#errorlensborder)
config.errorLens.padding.description: Padding of the inline message. Shows when `#poly.errorLens.messageBackgroundMode#` is `message`. [Demo](https://github.com/usernamehw/vscode-error-lens/blob/v3.29.0/docs/docs.md#errorlenspadding)
config.errorLens.borderRadius.descriptio: Border radius of the inline message. Shows when `#poly.errorLens.messageBackgroundMode#` is `message`. [Demo](https://github.com/usernamehw/vscode-error-lens/blob/v3.29.0/docs/docs.md#errorlensborderradius)
config.errorLens.messageTemplate.descrip:
Template of the inline message. Whitespace between the items counts.

- `$message`: the problem's message
- `$count`: how many problems are on its line, when more than one
- `$severity`: its prefix from `#poly.errorLens.severityText#`
- `$source`: where it comes from, such as `eslint`
- `$code`: its code
- `$lineStart`, `$lineEnd`: the lines it starts and ends on

An absent `$count`, `$source` or `$code` takes the characters attached to it along, so `($source)` leaves no empty brackets behind. [Demo](https://github.com/usernamehw/vscode-error-lens/blob/v3.29.0/docs/docs.md#errorlensmessagetemplate)
config.errorLens.messageMaxChars.descrip: Cut the inline message off after this many characters, which also keeps long messages from slowing the editor down. [Demo](https://github.com/usernamehw/vscode-error-lens/blob/v3.29.0/docs/docs.md#errorlensmessagemaxchars)
config.errorLens.maxInlineMessages.descr: When a file has more lines with problems than this, inline messages are drawn only for the lines in view and those around them. VSCode makes CSS rules for every distinct message, and thousands of them can freeze the editor for a long time. Line highlights, gutter icons, problem ranges, hovers and the status bar are not limited. `0` is no limit.
config.errorLens.severityText.descriptio: What `$severity` in `#poly.errorLens.messageTemplate#` becomes, by severity: error, warning, info, hint. [Demo](https://github.com/usernamehw/vscode-error-lens/blob/v3.29.0/docs/docs.md#errorlensseveritytext)
config.errorLens.messageEnabled.descript: Show the inline message, and the line's background with it. [Demo](https://github.com/usernamehw/vscode-error-lens/blob/v3.29.0/docs/docs.md#errorlensmessageenabled)
config.errorLens.messageBackgroundMode.n: Nothing: the message has only its text color.
config.errorLens.messageBackgroundMode.d: What is tinted by the problem's severity. [Demo](https://github.com/usernamehw/vscode-error-lens/blob/v3.29.0/docs/docs.md#errorlensmessagebackgroundmode)
config.errorLens.problemRangeDecorationE: Highlight the problem's whole range as well. [Demo](https://github.com/usernamehw/vscode-error-lens/blob/v3.29.0/docs/docs.md#errorlensproblemrangedecorationenabled)
config.errorLens.editorHoverPartsEnabled: What Error Lens adds to the editor's hover on a problem: the message, its source and code with copy buttons, and buttons to exclude it, open its rule's definition or docs, search the web for it, or disable its rule for the line.
config.errorLens.statusBarIconsEnabled.d: Show error and warning counts in the status bar, highlighted. [Demo](https://github.com/usernamehw/vscode-error-lens/blob/v3.29.0/docs/docs.md#errorlensstatusbariconsenabled)
Where the status bar counts sit: higher numbers go further left.
config.errorLens.statusBarIconsAlignment: Which side of the status bar the counts are on.
config.errorLens.statusBarIconsTargetPro: Every known problem, in every file.
Which problems the status bar counts.
config.errorLens.statusBarIconsUseBackgr: Highlight the status bar counts with a background; off, with their text color.
config.errorLens.statusBarIconsAtZero.de: What a count of zero does: `hide` hides it, `removeBackground` keeps it without its highlight.
config.errorLens.statusBarMessageEnabled: Show a problem's message in the status bar. [Demo](https://github.com/usernamehw/vscode-error-lens/blob/v3.29.0/docs/docs.md#errorlensstatusbarmessageenabled)
config.errorLens.statusBarMessagePriorit: Where the status bar message sits: higher numbers go further left.
config.errorLens.statusBarMessageAlignme: Which side of the status bar the message is on.
Color the status bar message by severity, with `poly.errorLens.statusBarErrorForeground`, `…WarningForeground`, `…InfoForeground` and `…HintForeground`. [Demo](https://github.com/usernamehw/vscode-error-lens/blob/v3.29.0/docs/docs.md#errorlensstatusbarcolorsenabled)
config.errorLens.statusBarMessageType.de: Which problem the status bar shows.
config.errorLens.statusBarMessageType.cl: The closest to the cursor of the most severe: an error further away comes before a warning nearby.
config.errorLens.statusBarMessageType.ac: The one on the cursor's line.
The one on the cursor's line closest to the cursor, following it along the line.
config.errorLens.statusBarCommand.descri: What clicking the status bar message does: `goToProblem` goes to the problem and opens its peek, `goToLine` only goes there, `copyMessage` copies the message.
config.errorLens.statusBarMessageTemplat: Template of the status bar message, with the variables of `#poly.errorLens.messageTemplate#`. Empty uses that one.
config.errorLens.replace.matcher.descrip: The regular expression a message is matched against.
config.errorLens.replace.message.descrip: The whole message for a match: `$0` is the match, `$1` its first group, and so on.
config.errorLens.replace.description: Rewrite messages. Each `matcher` is a regular expression, tried against the message ignoring case; the first that matches replaces the whole message with its `message`, where `$0` is the match and `$1`, `$2`… its groups. `[{ "matcher": "foo (.*)", "message": "just $1" }]` shows `foo bar` as `just bar`. [Demo](https://github.com/usernamehw/vscode-error-lens/blob/v3.29.0/docs/docs.md#errorlensreplace)
config.errorLens.transmute.target.messag: Matches a problem whose message contains this, ignoring case.
Matches a problem whose message matches this regular expression.
config.errorLens.transmute.target.source: Matches a problem from this source, such as `eslint` or `ts`.
config.errorLens.transmute.target.code.d: Matches a problem with this code, such as `@typescript-eslint/semi` or `6133`.
config.errorLens.transmute.severity.desc: The severity to show the problem with, which also decides the decoration it gets.
config.errorLens.transmute.decoration.li: Applies with light color themes only.
config.errorLens.transmute.decoration.da: Applies with dark color themes only.
config.errorLens.transmute.description: Change the severity or the look of particular problems. Each entry, under a name of your choosing, has a `target` (`message`, `messageRegex`, `source`, `code`: every one given has to match) and the `severity` or `decoration` to apply. [Demo](https://github.com/usernamehw/vscode-error-lens/blob/v3.29.0/docs/docs.md#errorlenstransmute)
config.errorLens.excludeByMessage.descri: Leave out problems by message: a string leaves out every message that contains it, ignoring case; an object's `regex` every message it matches (`flags` default to `iu`).
config.errorLens.excludeBySource.descrip:
Leave out problems by `source` or `source(code)`:

```json
[
	"eslint", // every problem from eslint
	"eslint(padded-blocks)", // eslint's padded-blocks rule
	"Pylance(reportUndefinedVariable)" // Pylance's reportUndefinedVariable
]
```
config.errorLens.excludePatterns.descrip: Leave out files matching these [glob patterns](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/editor/glob-patterns), such as `["**/*.{ts,js}"]`.
config.errorLens.excludeWorkspaces.descr: Leave out these workspace folders, by path. **Poly: Error Lens: Toggle Workspace in Disabled List** adds or removes the current one.
config.errorLens.disableLineComments.des: The comment **Poly: Error Lens: Disable Line** adds, by source, with `$code` for the problem's code. It goes on the line above; with `SAME_LINE` in it, at the end of the problem's own line: `"eslint": "// eslint-disable-line $code SAME_LINE"`.
config.errorLens.lintFilePaths.descripti: Where **Poly: Error Lens: Find Linter Rule Definition** looks for a rule, by source: [glob patterns](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/editor/glob-patterns) of the linter's configuration files, outside `node_modules`. `none` leaves a source out, and takes the hover's Definition and Disable line buttons away from its problems.
config.errorLens.searchForProblemQuery.d: The address **Poly: Error Lens: Search for Problem** opens in the browser, with the variables of `#poly.errorLens.messageTemplate#`.
config.errorLens.selectProblemType.close: The closest to the cursor of the most severe: an error further away comes before a warning nearby.
config.errorLens.selectProblemType.activ: The one on the cursor's line.
config.errorLens.selectProblemType.descr: Which problem **Poly: Error Lens: Select Problem** selects.
config.errorLens.light.description: Gutter icons for light color themes. Empty values fall back to the settings of the same name.
config.errorLens.light.errorGutterIconPa: Absolute path of the error gutter icon.
config.errorLens.light.warningGutterIcon: Absolute path of the warning gutter icon.
config.errorLens.light.infoGutterIconPat: Absolute path of the info gutter icon.
config.errorLens.light.hintGutterIconPat: Absolute path of the hint gutter icon.
config.errorLens.light.errorGutterIconCo: Color of the error icon in the shape and letter icon sets.
config.errorLens.light.warningGutterIcon: Color of the warning icon in the shape and letter icon sets.
config.errorLens.light.infoGutterIconCol: Color of the info icon in the shape and letter icon sets.
config.errorLens.light.hintGutterIconCol: Color of the hint icon in the shape and letter icon sets.
config.errorLens.delay.description: Wait this long (ms) before showing problems; `0` shows them at once. Anything below 500 counts as 500. `#poly.errorLens.delayMode#` says how it waits.
config.errorLens.delayMode.new: Messages disappear while you type, and come back once the document and its problems have been still for the delay.
config.errorLens.delayMode.old: A new problem appears after the delay; a fixed one disappears at once.
config.errorLens.delayMode.debounce: Every update waits until the problems have stopped changing for the delay.
config.errorLens.onSave.description: Update the decorations only on a manual save; an edit clears them until the next one.
config.errorLens.onSaveTimeout.descripti: How long (ms) after a manual save to draw the decorations, which gives the linters time to report.
config.errorLens.onSaveUpdateOnActiveEdi: With `#poly.errorLens.onSave#` on, still draw decorations when the active or visible editors change.
config.errorLens.enableOnDiffView.descri: Show decorations in diff editors as well, such as a git diff. [Demo](https://github.com/usernamehw/vscode-error-lens/blob/v3.29.0/docs/docs.md#errorlensenableondiffview)
config.errorLens.followCursor.allLinesEx: All except the one on the cursor's line.
config.errorLens.followCursor.activeLine: Only the one on the cursor's line.
config.errorLens.followCursor.closestPro: Only the closest to the cursor.
config.errorLens.followCursor.descriptio: Which problems are highlighted, by where the cursor is. [Demo](https://github.com/usernamehw/vscode-error-lens/blob/v3.29.0/docs/docs.md#errorlensfollowcursor)
config.errorLens.followCursorMore.descri: Adds to `#poly.errorLens.followCursor#`: with `activeLine`, this many lines above and below; with `closestProblem`, this many more problems. [Demo](https://github.com/usernamehw/vscode-error-lens/blob/v3.29.0/docs/docs.md#errorlensfollowcursormore)
config.errorLens.gutterIconsEnabled.desc: Show gutter icons, where breakpoints go. [Demo](https://github.com/usernamehw/vscode-error-lens/blob/v3.29.0/docs/docs.md#errorlensguttericonsenabled)
config.errorLens.gutterIconsFollowCursor: When `#poly.errorLens.followCursor#` is not `allLines`, still show gutter icons for every problem; only the line highlight and the message follow the cursor. [Demo](https://github.com/usernamehw/vscode-error-lens/blob/v3.29.0/docs/docs.md#errorlensguttericonsfollowcursoroverride)
config.errorLens.gutterIconSize.descript: Size of the gutter icons: `auto`, `contain`, `cover`, or a percentage such as `50%` or `150%` ([CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/background-size)). [Demo](https://github.com/usernamehw/vscode-error-lens/blob/v3.29.0/docs/docs.md#errorlensguttericonsize)
config.errorLens.gutterIconSet.default: Like the Problems panel's icons (old style).
config.errorLens.gutterIconSet.defaultOu: Like the Problems panel's icons (new style).
config.errorLens.gutterIconSet.borderles: Like the Problems panel's icons, without a border.
config.errorLens.gutterIconSet.squareRou: A filled square with rounded corners.
config.errorLens.gutterIconSet.letter: A letter: E, W, I, H.
config.errorLens.gutterEmoji.description: The emoji for each severity when `#poly.errorLens.gutterIconSet#` is `emoji`. [Demo](https://github.com/usernamehw/vscode-error-lens/blob/v3.29.0/docs/docs.md#errorlensgutteremoji)
config.errorLens.errorGutterIconPath.des: Absolute path of an image to use as the error gutter icon. [Demo](https://github.com/usernamehw/vscode-error-lens/blob/v3.29.0/docs/docs.md#errorlenserrorguttericonpath)
config.errorLens.warningGutterIconPath.d: Absolute path of an image to use as the warning gutter icon. [Demo](https://github.com/usernamehw/vscode-error-lens/blob/v3.29.0/docs/docs.md#errorlenserrorguttericonpath)
config.errorLens.infoGutterIconPath.desc: Absolute path of an image to use as the info gutter icon. [Demo](https://github.com/usernamehw/vscode-error-lens/blob/v3.29.0/docs/docs.md#errorlenserrorguttericonpath)
config.errorLens.hintGutterIconPath.desc: Absolute path of an image to use as the hint gutter icon. [Demo](https://github.com/usernamehw/vscode-error-lens/blob/v3.29.0/docs/docs.md#errorlenserrorguttericonpath)
config.errorLens.errorGutterIconColor.de: Color of the error icon in the shape and letter icon sets. [Demo](https://github.com/usernamehw/vscode-error-lens/blob/v3.29.0/docs/docs.md#errorlenserrorguttericoncolor)
Color of the warning icon in the shape and letter icon sets. [Demo](https://github.com/usernamehw/vscode-error-lens/blob/v3.29.0/docs/docs.md#errorlenserrorguttericoncolor)
config.errorLens.infoGutterIconColor.des: Color of the info icon in the shape and letter icon sets. [Demo](https://github.com/usernamehw/vscode-error-lens/blob/v3.29.0/docs/docs.md#errorlenserrorguttericoncolor)
config.errorLens.hintGutterIconColor.des: Color of the hint icon in the shape and letter icon sets. [Demo](https://github.com/usernamehw/vscode-error-lens/blob/v3.29.0/docs/docs.md#errorlenserrorguttericoncolor)
config.errorLens.removeLinebreaks.descri: Replace line breaks in inline and status bar messages with `#poly.errorLens.replaceLinebreaksSymbol#`.
config.errorLens.replaceLinebreaksSymbol: What a line break in a message becomes, with `#poly.errorLens.removeLinebreaks#` on.
config.errorLens.scrollbarHackEnabled.de: Keep inline messages from widening the editor into a horizontal scrollbar. The messages can then no longer be hovered. [Demo](https://github.com/usernamehw/vscode-error-lens/blob/v3.29.0/docs/docs.md#errorlensscrollbarhackenabled)
config.errorLens.decorations.description: Low-level decoration options, by key: `errorRange`, `warningRange`, `infoRange`, `hintRange`, `errorMessage`, `warningMessage`, `infoMessage`, `hintMessage`. The properties are VSCode's [decoration options](https://code.visualstudio.com/api/references/vscode-api#ThemableDecorationAttachmentRenderOptions): `backgroundColor`, `color`, `outline`, `border`… [Demo](https://github.com/usernamehw/vscode-error-lens/blob/v3.29.0/docs/docs.md#errorlensdecorations)
config.errorLens.ignoreDirty.description: Leave out files with unsaved changes, unless `files.autoSave` is `afterDelay`.
config.errorLens.codeLensEnabled.descrip: Show problems as code lenses above their lines as well. [Demo](https://github.com/usernamehw/vscode-error-lens/blob/v3.29.0/docs/docs.md#errorlenscodelensenabled)
config.errorLens.codeLensLength.descript: Shortest and longest a code lens's text can be, in characters: shorter is padded, longer cut off.
config.errorLens.codeLensTemplate.descri: Template of the code lenses, with the variables of `#poly.errorLens.messageTemplate#`.
config.errorLens.codeLensOnClick.searchF: Searches the web for the problem.
config.errorLens.codeLensOnClick.descrip: What clicking a code lens does.

config.syntax.updateCheck.enabled.descri: Periodically check GitHub Releases for a new poly-syntax-highlight, and install a new one without asking; only the window reload is left to you. An update also installs Poly (poly-lsp) when it is installed, and a release one of the two already installed in this window is not installed again.
config.syntax.updateCheck.intervalDays.d: Days between this extension's automatic update checks; 0 checks on every startup. Separate from Poly's own poly.updateCheck.intervalDays.
config.poly.description: All of Poly's settings, as one object. Poly keeps this block in your user settings.json: every key is listed with what it does, its allowed values and its default, and a key you have not set stays commented out. Uncomment a line to change it.
